questions: Do you have a known history of thyroid disease (such as Graves' disease or hyperthyroidism)?
Have you noticed your eyes appearing to bulge forward recently?
Do you experience double vision when looking at objects?
Do you have a history of diabetes mellitus?
Do you have a history of hypertension?
Did the double vision start suddenly or gradually?
Did the double vision start suddenly (over hours to days)?
Do you have a history of head trauma or recent surgery?

Do you have a history of migraine headaches?
orders: Perform the forced duction test to differentiate restrictive from paralytic strabismus.
Measure intraocular pressure in primary gaze and on upgaze (to check for elevation-induced IOP rise).
Examine the pupils for relative afferent pupillary defect (RAPD) and perform visual field testing by confrontation.
MRI of the orbits with fat suppression (STIR sequences) to evaluate for extraocular muscle enlargement and tendon involvement.
Bedside ice pack test (apply ice to the ptotic eyelid for 2 minutes and observe for improvement in lid elevation).
Serum thyroid function tests (TSH, Free T4) and Thyroid Stimulating Immunoglobulin (TSI).
